activeExperiments.hypothesis: Audit of 2,569 published articles shows OIC-tagged stories (10% of corpus) have a median regional-source share of 20% and only 51.4% include ≥1 regional outlet. The selector currently treats regional outlets as a soft tiebreaker only, so when feed clustering doesn't bundle a regional outlet into a story's cluster, the regional voice gets dropped. Adding an explicit selection-criteria item plus an internal-verification check that requires regional carry-through for OIC-tagged stories — drawing from the broader feed, not just the cluster — should raise ≥1 regional-source coverage on OIC stories from 51.4% to ≥80% over the 7-day window without dropping throughput. Token-neutral: prompt change only, no extra NewsAPI calls.
activeExperiments.oldValue: Muslim-world outlets listed under reader-aligned-sources tiebreaker only
activeExperiments.newValue: Explicit OIC-region carry-through rule + internal-verification check, with named recognized outlets per OIC country

guardrails.selectorTime: selector stage time must not climb >25% (~660s baseline) — extra feed scanning could slow it.

activeExperiments.hypothesis: Brief block adoption shows rank/sankey/treemap stuck at <2.5% of briefs over the past 7 days (3+3+7 = 13 of 286 briefs) despite the Apr 26 prompt overhaul that lifted timeline from 13 lifetime to 110 in one week. The remaining gap is the fabrication gate: it asks 'could I name peers WITHOUT inventing numbers?', which the model interprets as 'skip if I don't know exact values'. Timeline doesn't need numbers, so it cleared. Rank/sankey/treemap need values, so they default-skip. Reframing the gate to permit approximate magnitudes ('roughly half', '≈40%', '~$30bn') while still blocking fabricated specifics should unblock shape-correct adoption without raising fabrication.

activeExperiments.hypothesis: Title-echo rate has trended 53.8 → 49.1 → 40.0 over three weekly snapshots — declining at ~9pp/week but still 4× the <10% target. Reflection observed the rule 'nudges rather than blocks'. The current rule already includes a worked example (Microsoft pause); the missing element is a procedural self-check that forces evaluation. Adding 'redact title, re-read S1' as a mandatory pre-save check converts a description into a discrete action the writer model must perform, which should accelerate the decline.

activeExperiments.newValue: title-echo rule + mandatory redact-and-reread self-check before saving

history.notes: Freshness median dropped from 1.2-day baseline to 0 on evaluation day (well below ≤1.0 target). All guardrails met: multi-source 9 (≥4), sci-tech 34% (≥25%), publish count 8/cycle (exactly at minimum). Article throughput compressed slightly to 41/day vs 49–57 prior days, suggesting the tighter cap trims the feed on lighter news days — worth watching but within acceptable range. Keeping cap at 22.

history.hypothesis: Published multi-source rate is 22% overall (39% politics, 18% economy, 4% science, 6% tech) against an achievable ceiling of ~40% given current feed composition. Science and tech are structurally single-source (specialist outlets don't cluster into Event Registry events), so gains must come from politics and economy. The selector's current guidance ('at least half of politics+economy picks from multiSourceStories when available') is soft and not being enforced — actual politics+economy multi-rate is 31% (26/84) vs the 50% target. Converting the soft guidance to a hard floor (politics ≥ 2, economy ≥ 2 multi-source picks when the feed supplies them) with a 'note why rejected' escape hatch should raise economy multi% meaningfully without padding with weak stories. Token-neutral: prompt change only, no extra NewsAPI calls.

history.newValue: Multi-source floors when feed supplies them: politics ≥ 2 multi-source picks, economy ≥ 2 multi-source picks. Note rejected multi-source story in selection summary when dropping below floor.

history.notes: Evaluated 2026-04-21 to 2026-04-25 (4 days, ~20 cycles). Politics multi-rate: 0.39 → 0.41 (+5%). Economy multi-rate: 0.18 → 0.23 (+28%). Politics+economy combined: 0.31 → 0.336 (+8.4%). Overall: 0.22 → 0.239 (+8.6%). Direction improved on all measures; no guardrail metric degraded >20%. Target of p+e ≥ 0.45 was not reached — the hard-floor guidance raised economy multi-rate but the feed's multi-source supply (~9/cycle) constrains how high the rate can go. Keeping the change: it is a measurable improvement over the soft guidance and produces better editorial discipline. Publish count dipped to 7/cycle on Apr 25 (below the 8 guardrail), but this appears to be a one-day anomaly rather than a sustained trend.

queuedExperiments.hypothesis: Bench test on 3 stories (write-prompt.md A vs E variants, Sonnet 4.6 medium) showed +38% specificity score (9.67 → 13.33) when adding an explicit 'Numerical density' rule to the principles block. Production 60-article baseline computes 8.58 specificity, so even 30% bench-to-prod attenuation would yield a meaningful gain. The current Precision principle says 'lead with the specific' but doesn't enforce a count; making 'at least 3 numerical specifics' a hard rule should push the writer toward number-leading copy, which is the wire-style discipline the prompt already aims for.
queuedExperiments.parameter: Numerical density principle in writer principles block
queuedExperiments.oldValue: No explicit numerical-density rule; only Precision principle ('lead with the specific')
queuedExperiments.newValue: Add: '**Numerical density.** Every article must contain at least 3 numerical specifics — counts, dates, percentages, currency amounts, or named figures (e.g. "5,000 troops," "March 14," "20% of supply," "$120 a barrel"). A wire dispatch without numbers is opinion. If adding a figure would push the body over 350 chars, drop an adjective or compress a clause to make room — don't drop the number.'
queuedExperiments.targetMetric: specificity score (digits + proper-noun tokens per article body, computed by scripts/lib/quality-score.js)
